author: Jennie Bell
title: Why Is Everyone Still Walking in Running Sneakers? - NewsBreak
text:
By Jennie Bell ,
1 days ago The fitness craze is fueling fresh opportunity in the walking shoe market , but the category is still getting overlooked by some brands and retailers.
Brooks Just Updated One of Its Perennial Daily Running Shoes With Cutting-edge New Tech
“The pandemic changed a mindset in our country, and for the good,” said Dan Ungar, president of Mar-Lou Shoes in Cleveland. “People know that walking is good for them, and it’s quite pleasing to see people come through our door and say, ‘I need a good walking shoe. My friend/doctor told me to try on XYZ shoes.’”
Brenda Felger, owner, president and chief executive officer of Felger’s Footwear in Houma, La., said customers like the functionality of the products. “I believe that walking shoes are becoming popular because they offer stability features along with maximum cushion,” she said.
However, overwhelmingly, walkers are still gravitating to other performance footwear for various reasons, including aesthetics and lack of awareness.
“We sell mostly running footwear for town walking or pavement walking,” said Melissa Walker, owner and president of Walker’s Shoe Center in Lancaster, Ohio. “And a fair amount of our clientele purchase hiking products to walk in, especially trail shoes from Merrell , Keen and Oboz.”
Bruce Wesley, owner of Wesley’s Shoes in Chicago, added, “People just want comfortable shoes to both walk, run and train in.”
Many walkers opt for running styles like the Brooks Adrenaline GTS for aesthetic reasons. Courtesy of Brooks The numbers reflect the market’s volatility. Circana reported that, in the fourth quarter of 2025 , sales for walking shoes grew 9 percent in dollars and experienced the strongest unit surge in the performance sector. But sales have slowed in the first half of 2026, while the running category remains strong.
Here, the four retailers talk about what’s selling now and what they need next from brands.
How strong is consumer interest in walking in your stores? Dan Ungar: Walking in our store is huge. Our average consumer age for both men and women is late 60s to early 70s, so we skew mature and our customers are rarely running in their sneakers. They’re walking. And the interest continues to build.
Melissa Walker: Walking shoes have always been a strong category for us. We have lots of parks, a bike path people walk on and very close to us are state parks where there is good hiking.
Bruce Wesley: Walking shoes are part of our DNA. Not a day goes by when people don’t come in asking for walking shoes. Demand for walking shoes is strong across profiles.
Why are consumers still often buying other performance footwear to walk in instead of actual walking shoes? Brenda Felger: Consumers are buying other [categories], such as running and tennis sneakers, because the “walking” category has been pretty bare and most people don’t know the difference. Many of the features that became popular in running shoes have made their way into walking shoes. I see more products being created in this category and I believe it’s right for my consumer.
The New Balance 928 walking shoes is a longtime favorite in the category. Courtesy of New Balance D.U.: Our customers purchase running styles on the advice of friends, doctors and, of course, because of their presence on social media. We’ve seen a tiny uptick in “not runners.” But again, tiny. The main [focus] continues to be technical — or semi-technical — running patterns from the big names. Now, to be fair, we are seeing some tiredness from some makers. Consumers want freshness in the styles they’re accustomed to. They want fresh redesigns. Virtually every day our customers ask, “What’s new from XYZ brand?”
Has Miu Miu Found Its Next Big Sneaker to Follow Up Its New Balance Collaboration?
What are your bestsellers in the walking category? M.W.: Walking shoes that we still sell are the traditional white or black, like New Balance men’s and women’s 928 or Brooks Addiction walking shoes. These shoes provide comfort and support. In the past, New Balance had a walking product that was mesh and very comfortable for our customers to walk in. They changed those styles and some of our customers moved from walking shoes to running shoes at that time. We do very well with the Hoka Transport — one of my personal favorites. We also do well with the Brooks GTS [options].
D.U.: Hoka and Brooks continue to drive our walking and athletic business. They both offer our customers a wide variety of choices in good sizes and widths. New Balance is still the finest brand for their array of sizes and widths, however. The classic 928 walking shoe from New Balance continues to move the needle in a pure walking shoe. We are doing quite well with some walking styles from non-athletic brands, like Vionic and Clarks . They both have some terrific sneakers built for walking . The trouble is that those non-athletic brands are not on the radar of podiatrists. Brooks, Hoka, New Balance and SAS are. And people listen to their doctors.
Vionic’s new Hummingbird style is its lightest walking shoe ever. Courtesy of Vionic B.W.: New Balance, On and Hoka still lead the way. However, we are seeing some strong gains from lines like Joya, Ara and Sam Hubbard. What sets them apart is their stability, their size offerings, their turnaround time on deliveries and refilling.
What is the key to communicating the benefits of walking shoes to your customers? B.F.: My staff is trained on the features and benefits of all our products and communicates such to our consumer. That’s why they come to us. The first thing we do to communicate this is to listen — listen to what the customer is looking for and why. Then we respond.
M.W.: When we are helping a customer with fitting a shoe for walking, we go over all the benefits a walking shoe offers versus walking in a running shoe. We also encourage our customers to try both styles so they can feel the difference.
B.W.: Our sales reps are pretty knowledgeable on the latest technology of the shoe. And we have POP. That also addresses features of the products.
Is there more opportunity in walking, or is it maxed out? B.F.: Heading into the spring 2027 market, I’ve already seen a couple of vendors with increased offerings in the walking category, and I’ve booked some for the spring 2027 season. I will be looking for a few more in the category while at The Atlanta Shoe Market this August.
M.W.: There is more opportunity for companies with expanding walking shoes, but they need to make them lightweight, mesh and not orthopedic looking — like the Hoka Transport. New Balance made some styles that were great about five years ago, but for some reason they changed those shoes and we have customers who are still missing that shoe.
Hoka’s Transport walking sneakers are top sellers for retailers. Courtesy of Hoka D.U.: I don’t think the category is maxed out. In fact, I’d like to see Hoka and Brooks go after walking more than they do. Brooks has some good walking shoes but, let’s face it, they don’t have the good looks or light and airy feel of the Ghost or Adrenaline. And the look is very, very important to our customers, no matter their age. They want the good-looking styles that happen to be in the pure running category.
What do you want more of from brands? B.F.: I’d like to see “new” designs, not just taking an old running style and making it a walking silhouette. It needs to be versatile so that it can be used as an everyday shoe as well as for the walking routine. And it needs to be lightweight; no heavy, clunky styles.
D.U.: I would like to see more freshness. When some key brands create updates, oftentimes they’re not radically different. And this is a conundrum for them. Hard-core runners — and sometimes walkers — don’t want a big change to the model. It can disrupt them. But too often the updates are too stale. The fit can’t change, but materially, the shoes need to really look different.
B.W.: I would like to see more use of microfiber stretch uppers and softer napa leathers. I would also like to see more platforms and unit bottoms. Sorel does an excellent job with their sandals.
